instructions: Review each fictional case independently against Enterprise ATT&CK 20.1.
Record the most specific active technique only when an adversary action is established by the observations.
Record the evidence IDs and a reason. Use an empty mappings object for approved, prevented or insufficient events.
Complete this review without access to author labels, model responses, or scores.

records.E1: The service desk logged a routine shift handover.
records.E2: An incident examiner reconciled two session journals and confirmed that an outsider performed a completed staff-directory update under an existing Active Directory domain account.

records.E1: The service desk logged a routine shift handover.
records.E2: The domain account appeared in an alert, but the controller recorded a rejected sign-on. The only completed directory update came from the approved service account.

records.E1: Cloud activity records verified a completed session under the already-issued cloud billing account. The nominated owner and the incident panel confirmed that the operator had no consent.
records.E2: Facilities confirmed that the meeting room monitor was online.

records.E1: A cloud billing session was investigated because it looked unusual. The audit confirmed that the assigned billing delegate performed it under written approval.
records.E2: Facilities confirmed that the meeting room monitor was online.

records.E1: A separate stock ledger reconciled ordinary office supplies.
records.E2: The post-incident snapshot and change log confirmed an unapproved additional cloud administrator role was assigned to an existing account. The alert about session use was withdrawn.

records.E1: A separate stock ledger reconciled ordinary office supplies.
records.E2: A draft showed an additional cloud administrator role for an existing account. The reviewer confirmed the request was rejected and the role never took effect.

records.E1: The helpdesk reconciled the directory records and verified that an intruder disabled existing staff accounts, immediately preventing the owners from signing in.
records.E2: The schedule had an approved lunch break for the facilities team.

records.E1: The directory showed accounts disabled under the signed offboarding list. The affected employees' departures and the approved change were verified.
records.E2: The schedule had an approved lunch break for the facilities team.

records.E1: The service desk logged a routine shift handover.

records.E1: The service desk logged a routine shift handover.
records.E2: A desktop-image alert was traced to images generated by the approved usability test. They depicted a mock desktop and no incident capture occurred.

records.E1: The endpoint investigator verified the intruder copied stored project reports from the local workstation for collection. The record identifies the source as files already stored on that workstation.
records.E2: Facilities confirmed that the meeting room monitor was online.

records.E1: A report claimed a set of local reports was copied. The only source is a forwarded rumor, and the examiner could find no trusted read or copy event.
records.E2: Facilities confirmed that the meeting room monitor was online.

records.E1: A separate stock ledger reconciled ordinary office supplies.
records.E2: The investigation verified that an intruder collected messages directly from the organization's remote mailbox service. It found no collection from local mailbox files.

records.E1: A separate stock ledger reconciled ordinary office supplies.

records.E1: A forensic review identified an intruder gathering stored messages from a local mailbox archive on a workstation. The account's remote mail service showed no matching access.
records.E2: The schedule had an approved lunch break for the facilities team.

records.E1: An employee's local mailbox archive was included in a scheduled backup. Review linked the event to the authorized backup identity.
records.E2: The schedule had an approved lunch break for the facilities team.

records.E1: The service desk logged a routine shift handover.
records.E2: The workstation shut down at the start of a scheduled electrical maintenance window. The records trace it to the scheduled and authorized operation.

records.E1: The application health log and incident sign-off establish that the intruder deliberately terminated the payroll worker service. The host remained online and other services continued.
records.E2: Facilities confirmed that the meeting room monitor was online.

records.E1: The payroll service became unhealthy during a rollout. The cause was never corroborated, and the incident note does not confirm deliberate service termination.
records.E2: Facilities confirmed that the meeting room monitor was online.
